co_religion.descent_text: The ninth pitch ends on the summit of the Notch Spire. Drop back to the notch, then use the standard descent. From the notch, the standard descent is the West Gully, a third- to fourth-class talus gully reached by working north and uphill along a cairned, well-worn path from the spire; cliffs lie below that path, so stay on it. Snow can linger in the upper gully until midsummer, and the exposed traverse is a poor place in an electrical storm. Rappelling the west face from bolted stations near the notch is the other choice and takes two 60 m ropes for about three rappels. At the foot of the gully, retrace the approach past Lake Helene to Bear Lake.
co_religion.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the Fern Lake trail for roughly 3 miles to the saddle between Joe Mills Mountain and Notchtop. An unsigned but obvious trail on the left drops to Lake Helene. Circle the lake counterclockwise, then follow the braided trail uphill through a gully that can hold snow until midsummer, watching for cairns, to a small tarn at the foot of the south ridge. Religion is on the main east face of the Notch Spire. Look for the leftmost of three prominent roofed dihedrals slightly left of center, where the first pitch begins with a leap across a moat from a huge flat flake.
